Multiple held at today's ~18x because a data-center-heavy peer (Duke) trades ~17.8x forward, so peer demand evidence does not justify a premium re-rating while the 10-year is ~5.2%.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$62 NEE would trade ~13.5x NTM EPS, well below the ~16x sector and ~17.8x Duke despite faster growth. Even with the $2.30/share regulatory fee priced in, a rate-driven derating alone would not get there, so it would most likely mean a fundamental break: deal failure plus an equity raise or growth-guidance cut, a large Uri damages award, an FPL regulatory setback, or impairment in Energy Resources' backlog.

reasoning: Round 2. Stock is down ~23% from the May high of $98.75, mainly on the sector-wide rate shock (10y 5.24% on Sep 28, easing to 5.23% Sep 30 after the cooler PCE [23,24]; utilities ~16x and at a 3-year oversold extreme [10]) plus overhang from the all-stock Dominion deal [8] under a contentious Virginia review [5,7]. New in round 2: (1) NEE, not Dominion, pays a $4.83B (~$2.30/share) regulatory termination fee if the deal fails on regulatory grounds [26]. (2) The Sep 28-29 Oklahoma partial summary judgment finds NextEra Energy Marketing liable for Uri price gouging, after FERC dismissed NEE's jurisdiction petition [20,21,22]; damages await trial. I verified both. I probability-weight them at ~$0.8/share and add them in full to the bear case. On the supervisor's multiple test: the peer data-center demand evidence (Duke, Southern, AEP [12,13,14]) is real, but Duke trades ~17.8x forward [25], about NEE's 17.9x, so it supports holding ~18x and does not argue for a premium. Fair value is ~$80.8 (P/E $81.6, dividend yield $79.7, net of event costs), ~6% above spot. Scenario mean ~$79.8 (bear $59/25%, base $82/50%, bull $96/25%). The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$80 and ~21.5% sigma, near the 21% realized vol, with a slightly fatter left tail for regulatory and legal binaries. As the supervisor asked, I cut the upper tail (K=102 0.16->0.13, K=114 0.07->0.05) to match a flat-multiple base case. Sell-side targets are evidence of upside skew, not the answer.
